Figure 1:StereoVLM: from binocular geometry to spatial understanding and action.
(a) Monocular observations leave metric scale ambiguous.
(b) An illustrative example of language-grounded metric reasoning from
calibrated stereo observations.
(c) Stereo3D-Bench evaluates spatial understanding at three levels.
Disparity supervision improves depth generalization, while hierarchical geometric
supervision benefits broader 3D spatial reasoning and downstream VLA performance.

Figure 2:Construction and task hierarchy ofStereo3D-Bench.
(a) The main split is constructed from four stereo data sources.
Independently selected point- and object-level subsets contain 2,017
and 1,556 stereo pairs, respectively, yielding 94,546 question–answer instances.
(b) Representative queries and answer formats for eight tasks spanning
point-level geometry, object-level geometry, and object-level spatial reasoning.

Figure 3:StereoVLM architecture and instruction tuning.
StereoVLM jointly processes an ordered stereo pair and a textual query
to generate answers autoregressively, with focal lengthfxf_{x}and baselineBBprovided for metric reasoning. Full-parameter instruction tuning
interleaves point-level stereo instructions (15%), object-level stereo
instructions (10%), and general monocular and video instructions (75%).
The SFT loss is applied only to answer tokens.
Figure 4:Qualitative comparison of metric-depth predictions on Stereo3D-Bench.

Figure 5:Comparison of source-native and estimated left-view depth.
The first two rows show DROID examples and the last two show
Xperience-10M examples. Columns show the rectified left image, the
source-native depth, S2M2 depth, and FoundationStereo depth. Predicted
depth is converted from disparity using the physical focal length and
baseline released for each pair. All maps are aligned to the
rectified-left image; colors are normalized independently within each
row and should not be compared across rows. White denotes invalid depth in the corresponding map. Rectification borders are cropped for display.

Figure 6:Point-level reference filtering. The first two rows show DROID
and the last two show Xperience-10M. Green pixels in the second column
have S2M2 depth within 10% of the source-native depth and form the
benchmark validity mask. The third column shows the analogous
FoundationStereo agreement mask for comparison only; it is not used for
benchmark sampling. Red pixels in the final column lie within three
pixels of a ridge in the source-native disparity map. Rectification
borders are cropped for display.

Figure 7:Object references.
(a) Xperience-10M, using the estimated gravity-aligned frame.
(b) DROID, using the provided camera extrinsics.
In each pair, the left image shows the object mask and the right image projects the oriented box after it is written back to the left camera.

Figure 9:Qualitative effects of the strongest single-axis calibration
perturbations. Each row shows the fixed left image and query, the
right image after an L3 perturbation, and the metric depth produced
by FoundationStereo from the perturbed pair. Green circles mark
nominal correspondences, red points mark their locations after
perturbation, and yellow arrows show the induced displacement. Row
labels give the perturbation direction and its mean horizontal and
vertical displacement. FoundationStereo receives the complete
perturbed images; the common crop is applied only for display, and
all depth maps share the same color scale. The displayed DROID
example uses0.99∘0.99^{\circ}rotations and 21.2 mm translations;
perturbation magnitudes vary slightly with each pair’s scene geometry.

Figure 11:Qualitative dense depth results across three evaluation domains. Columns show the rectified left image, ground-truth depth, StereoVLM-2B with standard stereo input, the same StereoVLM-2B checkpoint with monocular input, and DepthVLM-4B. Rows are drawn from DROID, Xperience-10M, and the in-house OOD split.

Figure 12:Qualitative semantic results under correct stereo input.
Columns show the ground truth, StereoVLM-2B, and StereoVLM-8B.
Object-depth examples report optical-axis depth in meters and use
yellow boxes to indicate the queried objects. Semantic 3D OBB and
task-target examples show oriented 3D boxes projected into the
rectified-left image. Green, orange, and blue denote the ground truth,
2B prediction, and 8B prediction, respectively. Depth and semantic
OBB examples are from Xperience-10M, while task-target examples are
from DROID. Only the left-view visualization is displayed; predictions
are produced from the complete stereo pair.
